100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On September 13, 1926, the British government faced mounting criticism over its handling of the General Strike, as tensions flared between labor unions and industrialists. In the United States, the American Legion continued its push for veterans' benefits, while the stock market showed signs of volatility amid economic uncertainty. Meanwhile, in Germany, the political landscape remained unstable with ongoing debates over reparations from World War I.
